content.text: As a digital creator in Nigeria, you're no stranger to the frustration of Stripe and PayPal kicking you off their platforms. Despite being one of the fastest-growing economies in the world, Nigeria's financial infrastructure is plagued by high transaction fees, currency fluctuations, and restrictive payment processing policies. When your Stripe or PayPal account gets banned, you're left with a choice: either give up on selling digital products or invest in a true alternative. But what does that really mean, exactly? To understand the difference, let's break down what each option offers and how they compare.
What Each Option Actually Offers

When you use Stripe or PayPal, you're essentially renting a payment processing solution that's built on top of someone else's infrastructure. This means you have no control over the underlying tech, no ownership of your data, and limited customization options. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure like COREMERCH's Complete Builder Kit ($197) offers a base-layer solution that gives you complete control over your digital store, from hosting to payment processing. This means you can customize your stack to suit your needs, own your data, and build a scalable business that's not beholden to any single platform.

Stripe and PayPal have strict policies against operating in certain countries, including Nigeria. When you get banned, you're out of luck – unless you're willing to set up a foreign entity or use a workaround that compromises your security. Sovereign commerce infrastructure, on the other hand, is designed to operate independently of these restrictions. By using a self-hosted solution like COREMERCH's Complete Builder Kit, you can process payments and sell digital products without relying on a platform that might arbitrarily restrict your access.

Stripe and PayPal charge high transaction fees, often ranging from 2.9% + 30¢ per transaction to 3.4% + 30¢. These fees can quickly eat into your profit margins, especially if you're selling low-priced digital products. Sovereign commerce infrastructure, by contrast, offers much lower fees – often under 1% + a small flat rate. And because you own your data and payment processing infrastructure, you can also avoid the hidden costs associated with platform fees and currency exchange rates.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure offers a permanent structural alternative to rental solutions like Stripe and PayPal.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

When you use Stripe or PayPal, your payment processing and order fulfillment are managed by the platform's automated systems. While this can be convenient, it also means you have limited control over the delivery and fulfillment process. With sovereign commerce infrastructure, you have complete control over how your digital products are delivered to customers. You can also automate the payment processing and order fulfillment process using custom-built scripts and workflows – giving you a scalable and efficient business that's not dependent on manual intervention.
